definition: A training schedule technique that gradually reduces the learning rate over the course of training, often to help the model settle into a more precise, stable solution.
details: Learning rate decay schedules (such as cosine decay or step decay) are widely used in training deep learning models, balancing fast initial learning with fine-grained convergence later in training.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Learning Rate Decay — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
